articleTitle: Chatbot as a learning resource? Creating conversational bots as a supplement for teaching assistant training course
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering, Technology and Education (TALE)
abstract: One of the technologies that educators can leverage is the use of chatbots or conversational agent to support teaching and learning. Moreover, with the recent advancement in AI, companies like Google, IBM, and Amazon provide platforms that are focused on building conversation rather than the technicalities of computer programing, in particular, natural language processing. In this case study, we will look into the application of a simple rule-based chatbot, based on Google DialogFlow, in a teaching assistant training course run by a Center for Education Innovation at the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology. We will unpack the details of how a chatbot can be integrated into both online and face-to-face content to augment some of the challenges that can be encountered in teaching.

articleTitle: Automated English Digital Essay Grader Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering, Technology and Education (TALE)
abstract: Automatic essay grader is a program that is designed to grade an essay automatically. Some of automatic essay grader have been made using string kernel, word embedding and reinforced learning method. The objective of this research is to develop an application to help users in grading English digital essays. Grading is done based on 12 score features. Argumentative and narrative essays written by junior high school students are utilized as the dataset. By using XGBoost as the classifier, this research produces an automated essay grader with an average accuracy of 66.87%. Evaluation is conducted using 5-fold cross validation method.

articleTitle: A Conversational Assistant on Mobile Devices for Primitive Learners of Computer Programming
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering, Technology and Education (TALE)
abstract: According to eMarketer's survey, the penetration rate of smart phone in Taiwan is one of the top 5 countries in the world, around 77.6% of her population in 2018. Especially among youths, almost everyone has a smartphone. They use mobile devices ubiquitously and it causes problems regarding learning in classroom. Instead of restriction of using smart phones, we encourage students to utilize the devices for learning as frequent as possible. Therefore, a conversational assistant (chatbot) based on IBM Watson Assistant and Facebook Messenger is developed to help non-technical students as they are primitive to computer programming. At the development stage, students appreciate the assistant as an “first-aid” about the course materials and suggest that it should provide more helps about programming logics. In the progress into the stage of test, we will cyclically analyze the conversations between the assistant and users and identify the improvements for better instructional design. The controlled experiment method is utilized to tell if the chatbot could improve the students' engagements and interests to programming for the first version of chatbot.

articleTitle: Learning Analytics in Augmented Reality : Blueprint for an AR / xAPI Framework
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering, Technology and Education (TALE)
abstract: Learning Analytics in flat web platforms is rather commonplace, but recording learner performance from immersive real-world experience still poses a challenge. With this study, we break ground and show that Learning Analytics for Augmented Reality are possible and we outline how an according system can be implemented. We describe a novel framework for competency-based workplace Learning Analytics and document the required components with regards to software, hardware, and their configuration. Thereby, we discuss key design decisions and lessons learned from the implementation of the framework, drawing from the experience of the EU project Learning Analytics in Augmented Reality (LAAR), which provided the environment and context for this work. Most notably, this included testing the technologies in realistic scenarios in vocational training of stage technicians. Finally, we conclude the paper with a summary of the work done and an outlook on possible extensions for researchers wishing to build on our work.

articleTitle: A Pedagogy that Uses a Kaggle Competition for Teaching Machine Learning: an Experience Sharing
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering, Technology and Education (TALE)
abstract: This paper proposes a pedagogy with the use of a Kaggle competition for teaching machine learning based on the principles of game-based learning and social constructivism. The pedagogy is devised based on the teaching experience of a machine learning subject with master students at our university. The pedagogy is formulated as a 7-step online competition-based teaching model. In the teaching model, a Kaggle competition is organized to be game-like so as to make the learning more engaging and fun. Further, a social learning environment is provided to support the social interaction needs in the learning. Based on our teaching experience of the machine learning subject, the teaching model with the use of a Kaggle competition was successful in enhancing the motivation and learning of the students. In general, students were more motivated to explore different ways and apply advanced techniques to further improve their solutions, found the experience challenging and fun, and had a deeper understanding of the application of the concepts and algorithms they learned to solve real-word problems. It is believed that our experience is a strong indication that the use of the teaching model to run a Kaggle competition can be a highly effective method for teaching machine learning. The teaching model can be extended to the teaching of other computer science and engineering related subjects, such as bioinformatic subjects.

articleTitle: Blockchain-based Learning Credential Verification System with Recipient Privacy Control
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering, Technology and Education (TALE)
abstract: Various forms of learning credentials play an important role in society. For example, a degree certificate is usually required to apply for many jobs. Currently, paper-based learning credentials such as diploma or degree certificates are still widely used. However, proof of such credentials' authenticity has become increasingly more difficult in recently years due to availability of low-cost desktop publishing tools. Recently, a blockchain-based digital certificate issuing and verification system has been proposed to address these problems. However, existing blockchain-based certification verification solutions have a few shortcomings in common. One of them is the lack of mechanism to control the amount of information and anonymity exposed during the verification process. This paper proposed a blockchain-based learning credential verification system, where a credential recipient can control the amount of credential-related information to be exposed during the verification process. The proposed solution makes use of a Merkle tree to encode causal relationship among pieces of information the credential is composed of. The abstract data model built on top of the binary Merkle tree has been proposed so that a recipient can choose to disclose part of the credential information, including the recipient profile. This means it is possible for credential verification to be performed anonymously. This can be achieved without increasing blockchain transaction cost and complexity. Example of use case scenarios that require such anonymous verification are described.

articleTitle: Comparison of Data Mining Classification Algorithms for Student Performance
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering, Technology and Education (TALE)
abstract: Student performance has an important role to measure student quality. Student quality can be measured through predictions of student performance. Prediction can be done using data mining techniques. One technique that can be used is the classification method. The research aims to find out which classification model has the best performance related to student performance data. The data used is taken from UCI Machine Learning, namely student performance. The study used seven methods, namely K-nearest neighbor, classification and regression trees, naïve bayes, adaboost, extratree, bernaoulli naïve bayes, random forest. The technology used to compare the seven methods uses Python programming. Testing the performance of methods using cross validation. The results of this study are the comparison of student performance classification algorithms on student math, namely K-Nearest Neighboring of 86.52%, classification and regression tests of 86.08%, naïve bayes of 84.78%, adaboost of 88.04%, extratree of 81.30%, bernaoulli naïve bayes of 79.34%, random forest E of 87.82%, random forest G of 89.78%. Based on these results we know that the best classification method is the random forest G of 89.78%.

articleTitle: CHAT: a Cultural Heritage Adaptive Tutor
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering, Technology and Education (TALE)
abstract: The world of distance education is enriching with new tools able to improve the training process. Modern eLearning environments do not simply aim to reproduce the typical processes of the world of traditional education but seek to enrich them thanks to the support of new technologies. In this scenario, the introduction of the Chatbots is interesting. Chatbots are software designed to simulate a conversation with a human being, through sophisticated natural language processing systems, and can support students making the training process more adaptive. In this paper an educational chatbot, CHAT, is presented. This chatbot is able to support students in the study of Cultural Heritage. Through natural language processing techniques and inferential approaches, the proposed Chatbot provides learning contents having a conversation with the students and understanding what their main training needs are. The Chatbot was used in a real context, the archaeological parks of Paestum, Herculaneum and Pompeii where the students can use it obtaining training contents contextualized to their training needs. The results obtained, in terms of student satisfaction, were very satisfactory.

articleTitle: Motivation as Basis for Building Infrastructure for Hardware MOOCs
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering, Technology and Education (TALE)
abstract: With advancements in technological tools, e-learning/distance methods such as MOOCs are now mainstream and no longer just trends [1]. For a “hardware MOOC,” i.e. a MOOC that requires hardware infrastructure apart from minimal tools required to access web technologies, various factors are key to participation in a MOOC. This work studies “marketing” factors in a hardware MOOC. Our work is for any agency attempting to engage with colleges in India and such developing countries, where it is needed to set up infrastructure for distance education. It is important for us to identify at the outset colleges likely and not so likely to setup infrastructure. This helps us maximize the return on our effort, in reaching out to colleges. e-Yantra is a robotics outreach project based out of Indian Institute of Technology Bombay and the e-Yantra Lab Setup Initiative builds the basis for imparting effective engineering education by creating standardized infrastructure and by training teachers in colleges. Principal Component Analysis and Logistic Regression are used to study success factors at the college and process levels in college participation in a hardware MOOC.

articleTitle: Learning Networking by Reproducing Research Results in an NS-3 Simulation Networking Laboratory Course
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering, Technology and Education (TALE)
abstract: In the past two years, the undergraduate networking laboratory course at our university has been redesigned in a learning-by-doing approach. We have carefully selected eight papers covering different networking topics and designed corresponding experiments for over 50 students to reproduce the research results in the NS-3 simulation platform. In this paper, we present the design of an NS-3 simulation based networking laboratory course by reproducing research results. The course curriculum and experiment design are introduced, the topics of which include wireless networking, software defined networking, and artificial intelligence algorithms in NS-3 platform. The proposed course has been implemented in our university with an online NS-3 lab environment, and fruitful results and positive feedback have been received from both students and teachers. This course aims to teach both engineering rigor and critical thinking for undergraduate students, moreover, help the students to understand key concepts of advanced topics in networking and obtain hand-on experiences in conducting network simulations, which are crucial for their future career or research.

articleTitle: Board Game Design for Python Programming Education
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering, Technology and Education (TALE)
abstract: In the traditional education system, most students sit and listen to a teacher's oral presentation. However, it is often difficult to increase student interest in learning using this method. Most students often become distracted during the sessions. A set of board games were designed and used in after-class learning to increase students' learning motivation. When playing the games, students had discussions with team members and learned from each other. Therefore, students learned and taught mutually. Studies have indicated that board games can be useful in learning Python programming. Thus, the proposed board games can promote programming concepts and solve problems in learning programming. According to the results, the proposed board games exhibited an excellent influence on student's learning goals.

articleTitle: Code Free Bot: An easy way to jumpstart your chatbot!
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering, Technology and Education (TALE)
abstract: Advancement in technology and innovation in teaching such as chatbot and extended reality can be daunting for teachers but as an educator, we need to leverage on these advancements to respond to the changes and challenges in the teaching and learning landscape. There are a number of tools available for teachers to use to overcome the challenges, and one of them is the application of artificial intelligence (AI) but creating a chatbot requires complex computer programming skills, and it is usually built from scratch to fit the intended educational purpose. This practice makes it difficult for teachers to adapt existing systems or to attempt in creating a similar version. In this workshop, we will be sharing our experiences gained from developing various chatbots for higher education using a commercial platform that can jumpstart your chatbot.

articleTitle: Facial Recognition Development to Detect Corporate Employees Stress Level
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering, Technology and Education (TALE)
abstract: Technology has developed so well even to the point where machines can recognize our faces. There many APIs and algorithms out there that can recognize human faces. These APIs or algorithms is called Artificial Intelligence or AI. As modern civilian life in modern society, AI has been used so many times and developed into something more. This time, we proposed an idea to recognize motions and emotions on human faces to detect their stress levels. Companies nowadays need to have something that can know how their employees are feeling or think about their work. This program works by taking an image input from mounted cameras on the office’s monitor. However, before that, the program must have been trained first to recognize faces and emotions. For this, the eigenfaces algorithm is used. After the input is received, then the program will process the image received and extract the features from the images such as eyes, nose, mouth, etc. to detect if there are faces and also the emotions of the face. After that, the features extracted will be matched with the features in the database to give an output of the percentage of stress.

articleTitle: Design of A Web Development Attitudes Survey
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering, Technology and Education (TALE)
abstract: This paper presents a work-in-progress project on the development of a web development attitudes survey (WAS). Built on established attitudes instruments in natural science and computer science, the WAS consists of 35 items to measure 7 constructs of students' attitudes towards web development: confidence, motivation, gender, usefulness, knowledge & learning style, self-reliance, and context. In a pilot study, we administered an online form of the WAS to the students in a small-size web development course at the beginning and the end of the semester. Comparison between the pre-course and post-course average scores demonstrated noticeable changes in the confidence, knowledge & learning style, self-reliance and context constructs. In the next step we will validate the WAS with a large student cohort.

articleTitle: A Hybrid-based Architecture for Web Service Selection
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering, Technology and Education (TALE)
abstract: With the rapid growth of Web services in recent years, it is very difficult to choose the suitable web services among those services that offer similar functionality. Choosing the right web service does not only incorporate the issue of finding a Web service base on their functionalities, but also assessing quality aspects of those services. Quality of services (QoS) is considered a distinguishing factor between similar web services and plays a vital role in web service selection. The aim of the model is to evaluate and rank the alternatives consisting of conflicting criteria or criteria with different QoS requirements. To address this issue, this study proposes a model for determining the most suitable candidate web service by integrating AHP (Analytic Hierarchy Process) and VIKOR (Vlsekriterjumska optimizacija I KOmpromisno Resenje) methods. AHP method computes the weights assigned to QoS criteria using pairwise comparison. Thereafter, the ranking of the web services, according to a user preferred criteria, is obtained using VIKOR method. Finally, a JAVA application was implemented using AHP and VIKOR methods. To show and substantiate the proposed model, data from QWS dataset is used.

articleTitle: What is this sound in dB? Pilot study on measuring the degrees of understanding of sound level in university students
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering, Technology and Education (TALE)
abstract: In this paper, for proposing appropriate information disclosure method of noise conditions, the objective is to grasp the degree of understanding to the size of the sound in the persons except the experts of acoustics. In particular, as an attempt to measure the degree of understanding of the loudness of university students, we measured the degree of understanding using the loudness chart kit developed by ourselves in lecture course. As a result, they commonly regarded the sound volumes of the rocket and the take-off of the airplanes as first or second loudest, but the subjective ranks of other sound sources were completely different among them. Some of the students who seem to have no knowledge at all about the sound source answered unreality values entirely.

articleTitle: Academic Success in 1st-year Engineering Students: Key Factors
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering, Technology and Education (TALE)
abstract: This work-in-progress research to practice paper analyzes how previous personal, social and academic variables converge in the explanation of students' academic performance, during the 1st year of Engineering courses. A sample of 737 1st year students of Engineering courses in a Portuguese public university was considered. Students age ranging from 16 to 41 years old (M = 18.29, SD =2.01), having entered the university with a GPA ranging from 154.6 to 200.0 (M =154.60, SD=18.10). Two measures of academic achievement were taken into account in this study: the number of subjects/curricular units successfully completed at the end of the 1st semester, and the average of the marks obtained in the approved curricular units at the end of the 1st year. In terms of predictors, we considered sex, age, parentś academic education, course and university option and access GPA. The regression analysis shows that GPA and sex have a higher impact on academic achievement. These data deserve attention from institutions and professors since some students access their courses without the necessary level of academic competencies, motivation and vocational career definition which justifies the need for diagnosing and levelling students' background and personal characteristics. It is also important because several students are not in their first option institution/course, which also impacts their adjustment process to the University.

articleTitle: Lecture Notes on the Relationship between the Power Spectrum Estimated by MVDR and CBF
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering, Technology and Education (TALE)
abstract: Power spectrum density estimation is a quite important tool in signal processing, from which we can analyze the frequency components of the random signal. CBF and MVDR are classical and modern power spectrum estimation methods respectively. Both of them can achieve ideal performance under certain conditions. Here we discuss the relationship between MVDR and CBF on the power spectrum function. Interestingly, we found that when the observation vector contains no more than two frequency components, CBF and MVDR power spectrum will peak at the same frequencies, and the peaks are the same. We hope that the results of this lecture notes can give some inspiration to students who are studying digital signal processing.

articleTitle: Enhancing the Classification Performance of Students Behavior on Serious Game using Discretization-based k-NN
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering, Technology and Education (TALE)
abstract: Data relating to the serious game interaction in the education area can be mined to find the students' behavior indicating the understanding of the specific subject. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first research to improve the classification performance of students' behavior on a serious game using k-NN based on the discretization method. The discretization method applied is unsupervised discretization called equal frequency. Then, we combine on k-NN with Manhattan as a distance metric. Additionally, we evaluate the performance using the cross-validation. Then, we analyze the result using the general classification metric, the sieve diagram, and ROC. The experimental result shows that the combination of k-NN and the discretization method with 5-intervals can achieve the highest level of all metrics and the widest Area Under Curve (AUC). This indicates that this proposed method can improve a higher performance than the k-NN without discretization.

articleTitle: Mobile Application Development to Mitigate the Risk of Earthquake
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering, Technology and Education (TALE)
abstract: Indonesia is prone to natural disasters such as an earthquake. Many people are clueless regarding what to do when an earthquake occurs. An earthquake has caused a more devastating outcome due to it being able to lead to other hazards. The idea of developing a mobile application surfaced by reading and receiving inspiration from the previous research. Previous research has been implementing different kinds of ways to alert people regarding the upcoming earthquake. The development of a mobile application to provide a platform that will assist people with information on what to do in times of before, during, and after the earthquake. Therefore, people will have a source that they can turn to when seeking information about the steps to be done when an earthquake occurs. Besides, providing information apropos to earthquakes, the mobile application will send further alerts to the people that are in that specific area. Moreover, people will be able to be aware of the particular areas that they are in. The alerts sent will give information to the people so that they could evacuate to safety as soon as possible before the upcoming earthquake occurs.

articleTitle: The use of Microframework for Portable and Distributed ePortfolio Development
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering, Technology and Education (TALE)
abstract: ePortfolio is an essential tool used for track and evaluates the learning process. This paper presents the current development of a web-based ePortfolio system that has been developed with Microframework. ePortfolio commonly used as a tool to track and evaluate student's artifacts as a result of the course assignment. Furthermore, ePortfolio is needed for lecturers who have been implementing Project-Based Learning (PBL) and Lab-Based Education (LBE). On the other hand, the lack of internet access that still an issue in Indonesia as developing countries ePortfolio needs to be accessed in both online and offline conditions. The proposed method is to develop a web-based application using python based micro-framework. The web-based application is to enable users to use in offline condition (no internet access). As a result, a web-based application that will be used for both students and lecturers to upload and evaluate the uploaded artifacts and synchronize its contents to the existing University Information Systems. As part of the development process, the proposed ePortfolio has been tested on a mini device installed Access Point (AP). With this approach, lecture and student could use the web-based ePortfolio in the classroom with no internet conditions. Both users need to synchronize the artifact to the ePortfolio server in a distributed manner when the mini device is connected to the existing university ePortfolio.

articleTitle: Figure Drawing Method Based on Human Motion Using Pictogramming
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering, Technology and Education (TALE)
abstract: We have been implementing a programming tool for novices called “Pictogramming,” which has been released on the web. In this application, parts of a human-shaped pictogram can be moved using a command sequence called the “Pictogram Animation Command.” The application also enables the drawing of the movement history of a body and this drawing is called the “Pictogram graphics”, which is similar to turtle graphics. This paper presents extend “Pictogram graphics” to draw using the movement history of specified body parts, called “Human Motion Drawing”. Through this method, various figures can be drawn by sequentially or concurrently combining certain simple commands. We conduct the some lessons with 2-class of 80 second-year junior high school students to evaluate the effectiveness of this method by SD (Semantic Differential) scale method and analyzing free form text. We found the result of the lesson which learned by this proposed method was well as rest of lessons.

articleTitle: Pipelined MIPS Simulation: A plug-in to MARS simulator for supporting pipeline simulation and branch prediction
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering, Technology and Education (TALE)
abstract: This paper presents the design and implementation of a Microprocessor without Interlocked Pipeline Stages (MIPS) pipelined simulator build on top of the MIPS Assembler and Runtime Simulator (MARS) as a plug-in. The MARS Simulator is a lightweight interactive development environment (IDE) for programming in MIPS assembly language, intended for education-level use. This plug-in called “Pipelined Simulator and Branch Explainer (PBSE)” provides the MARS users with the ability to simulate a pipelined processor execution of MIPS assembly instruction which the original MARS simulator does not support. The tool also provides additional functionality as such Branch Prediction. With the use of the plug-in, MARS users can better analyze the assembly codes executed in a pipelined processor with branch prediction and improve their understanding of Computer Architecture.

articleTitle: Analysis of Learning Effect using a SQL Learning Support System in the Class
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering, Technology and Education (TALE)
abstract: This study presents analytical results of the relationship between student grade in a database class and frequency of SQL execution using our SQL learning support system. In the class of “database system”, students are required to learn SQL, which is a standard query language for the relational database system, as the fundamental knowledge of this subject. Through the SQL learning, students can learn the practical database skills for design and operation of database system. Therefore, in the database class, it is clearly important to lead students to correct understanding of SQL for nurturing skilled engineer of the database system. For this purpose, we have developed a web-based learning system for supporting SQL practice. In this study, using this SQL learning support system, we recorded and analyzed learning histories of students in the class conducted in 2015. The analytical results showed that there was a strong correlation between the frequency of SQL execution and the grade of final examination.

articleTitle: The Challenges of Implementing Online Learning in Secondary Education
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering, Technology and Education (TALE)
abstract: This study aims to explore the challenges of implementing technology in secondary schools, especially in terms of pedagogy. Regarding the needs of students in the industrial revolution 4.0, the researchers ask the ways of schools to implement technology and online learning to answer the said needs. Using Neuro research method, the study collects and analyse data using a literature review. The researchers explain the implementation of technology in education and how the educational system in Indonesia support the needs. The study reveals that technology and online learning is required and relevant for teaching in Indonesian context because it is the characteristics of the students in the generation. However, there are some challenges including the skills of teachers in technology and in pedagogy, the management of technology that answered the needs of students, and the system that encounters a problem because it is government-centred (central policy in the curriculum). Regarding online learning, there is no specific regulation for the implementation of online learning in secondary education. The recommendation is related to the system and legal support of the government to develop the online learning implementation in secondary school.

articleTitle: Web Recommended System Library Book Selection Using Item Based Collaborative Filtering Method
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering, Technology and Education (TALE)
abstract: The recommendation system is one feature that is widely used by software today. The recommendation system is Beneficial for users to make it easier for users to make a book selection by providing book recommendations that may be following the desired book preferences. The recommendation system in this research uses the Item Based Collaborative Filtering method, where this method is the result of combining Collaborative Filtering and Item Based. Collaborative Filtering uses the rating matrix to calculate ratings, and Item Based uses book attributes to calculate similarity attributes between books.The collaborative filtering method has been used successfully in several applications. The Collaborative Filtering method predicts user preferences for items in a word-of-month manner, i.e. user preferences are determined by considering opinions in the form of preference ratings.Based on the results of tests conducted, the minimum MAE generated by the system is 0.018 with a maximum accuracy of 99.63% contained in the first test, meaning that the more variable data rating data, the higher the MAE value generated.

articleTitle: Gamified Flipped Classroom Learning Approach: A Case Study of AJ University
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering, Technology and Education (TALE)
abstract: From the past studies, we know that a well-designed game-based or flipped classroom or gamified flipped classroom learning approaches can enhance student engagement, reduce topic complexity, enable clear task orientation, improve session effectiveness, and increase student satisfaction. We have examined it through our planned course delivery model with its foundation in the gamified flipped classroom learning approach. A six-week IT foundation course delivered to undergraduate students with majors in accounting, finance, marketing, and management. Two groups of students for this study: (1) an experimental group of 62 students with gamified course experience, and (2) a control group of 37 students through traditional learning. We performed a descriptive analysis mixed research approach to compare the results of the experimental with the control groups. The results showed a positive impact of the proposed course delivery model based on formal assessment marking, independent learning behavior, and improved class participation. However, this research has also identified various technological and delivery challenges faced by the participants, including students and teachers.

articleTitle: A Systematic Literature Review on the roles of Interest and Motivation in STEM Education
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering, Technology and Education (TALE)
abstract: The decreasing number of students opting for STEM subjects and careers has led to the implementation of various strategies to get them interested in STEM. Despite such efforts, the number of graduates majoring in STEM continued to decline. Several researchers believe that interest and motivation are two key factors that could lead students to choose STEM as their career paths. Hence, this systematic literature review aims to review related studies substantiating the roles interest and motivation play in STEM education and how these two key factors can help attract more students to choose STEM subjects and careers to meet the nation's demands.

articleTitle: Using Selective Syntactic Online Compiler to Promote Programming Learning
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering, Technology and Education (TALE)
abstract: It is an important problem that let students do practices according to course objectives, but not take tricky shortcuts. For example, one can use build-in libraries to solve a sorting question and does not really understand the fundamental principles of the sorting algorithm. To avoid this kind of problems, our research team proposed the python-based Selective Syntactic Compiler (pySSC) to limit students can only apply permitted grammars. Also, we build an instant, interactive and online compiler for the pySSC usage. Teachers can use the pySSC platform to some specific syntax constraints and then students can use this platform to build codes as well as to get real-time feed-backs. Finally, our research team also executed a questionnaire-based survey to evaluate the performance of the pySSC in terms of three types of affordances, namely cognitive, perceived and functional affordances.

articleTitle: Numerical Control Plotter For Direct-To-Blank Substrate Tracing Of Conductive Ink For Electronic Education Purposes
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering, Technology and Education (TALE)
abstract: The project study was conducted to develop a prototype that directly draws conductive traces onto a non-conductive surface. The project study also aimed to test commercially available conductive inks and against different substrates to find the workable materials for the prototype's application.

articleTitle: Enhancing Teaching Effectiveness in Mobile Application Development with Structured Practice
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering, Technology and Education (TALE)
abstract: Mobile application development is gaining increasing attention due to the rapid growth of the mobile technologies and mobile application market. Many universities are putting effort on integrating mobile application development into curriculum. The complexity and consistent changing in mobile development environment brings barriers and difficulties in course development. This paper describes how to enhance teaching effectiveness and engage students actively in mobile application development class through structured practice. The proposed structured practice features two levels of hands-on practice: first, prepare students with foundational knowledge and skills by having them follow the instructor on developing base applications; second, the philosophy of challenge-based learning is adopted in practice, where students are encouraged to independently work on developing implementations for applications with gradually increased complexity. Student feedbacks and performance have indicated the structured practice is an effective way of teaching mobile development which not only enhances the teaching effectiveness but also provides students a positive learning experience. Details of course design and project samples are provided to assist audiences in understanding the usage of structured practice and help with the developing of mobile application development courses.

articleTitle: Online Micro-Modules Library Production for Fundamental Programming Courses with Active Learning
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering, Technology and Education (TALE)
abstract: Engineering faculties encounter many challenges when teaching first-year programming courses. One of challenges is that the first-year students have grossly different levels of programming experience. We would also like to standardize the online programming training across different programming languages. As a result, Online Micro-Modules Library (OML) for fundamental programming courses are being developed in our university. This paper outlines the production process and preliminary outputs for the OML development, based on the Analyze, Design, Develop, Implementation and Evaluation (ADDIE) model. Various online learning tools, as well as active learning components, are employed in the OML. The development process reveals interesting insights and offers possibilities of applying the system design to other engineering disciplines.

articleTitle: Improving High School Girls’ 21st Century Skills: Design, Implementation, Assessment on megaGEMS Research Camp
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering, Technology and Education (TALE)
abstract: This work-in process paper presents a six-week high school level summer Science, Technology, Engineering, Art, Mathematics (STEAM) research camp, called megaGEMS Research Camp which is modeled after the National Science Foundation (NSF) Research Experience for Undergraduates (REU). We are presenting the curriculum, students' research projects, teaching methodology, assessment framework, and interview findings in this paper. In the summer of 2019, nine high school girls participated in the six-week summer research camp and worked on five Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics (STEM) related projects. The camp aims to provide high school girls with a better understanding of what research is and how research is carried out, which in turn may aims to improve their research skills, STEM interests, and 21st century skills. Based on the interview data, we found (1) students had a better understanding of the term research, (2) the camp created a valuable and supportive learning community, and (3) the camp learning experiences can be applied in their future advanced learning in high school and college.

articleTitle: AIGO: A comprehensive platform for cultivating AI talent using real-world industrial problems
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering, Technology and Education (TALE)
abstract: This paper introduces a platform, AIGO, aiming to cultivate AI talents, and enabling them to solve real-world industrial problems. The platform is composed of three blocks: (1) Competition: Designed for training AI practitioners by holding competitions to solve real-world problems. (2) Learning: Offering courses in a diverse range of theory and practical techniques of AI and complementing the insufficient abilities of AI practitioners. (3) Community: Offering both online and offline connection towards all the participants of the platform and providing a larger scale and population to join both Competition and Learning. So far we have seen positive feedback on both problems number and the number of competition participants. The number of problems we have collected increased from 50 (first competition) to 100 (third competition), and the number of competition participants increased from 138 (first competition) to 320 (second competition).

articleTitle: Implementation of Mobile game for Religion Learning
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering, Technology and Education (TALE)
abstract: Currently, the growth of information and technology is rapid. It makes a lot of things in various fields including education becoming more effective and efficient. In education, one of its implementation which is a game is proven to be a useful tool to support conventional teaching methods and bring a more natural understanding of learning materials. Moreover, as a product of the popular culture in modern society, video game mirrors the general culture practice in real life and reflects it via its own culture inside the game. This makes a video game can give a contribution to the social construction of reality as it affects the player's view towards learning in real life and vice versa. From there, we see that there is an opportunity for learning about religion to be supported by its utilization to provide an interactive and fun learning experience. In this paper, we discuss how a video game is implemented to support religious learning. The game was developed with the scrum method where we surveyed to gather the user requirements before the design step. The game design was made by using the use case diagram and storyboard, and it was built using Unity version 2017.3.0f3.

articleTitle: Design of Online Learning Mobile APP for the Elderly Based on Attention, Relevance, Confidence, and Satisfaction (ARCS) Motivation Model
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering, Technology and Education (TALE)
abstract: Currently, exploring the application method of Attention, Relevance, Confidence, and Satisfaction (ARCS) motivation model in the design of online learning APP for the elderly helps to improve the learning performance and user experience and to satisfy learning need better. Methods are through the observation, questionnaire and interview, and the user research which was carried out for the elderly users collected qualitative data and quantitative data of elderly users. Combining the online learning products and ARCS motivation model helps to summarize the design method of the online learning mobile APP for the elderly users, and explore the design of the mobile APP. In the application design of the elderly related to learning, the psychological characteristics and physiological characteristics of the elderly, should be fully considered. The ARCS motivation model and the user experience related rules should be combined to achieve the purpose of improving the online learning initiative and the learning efficiency of the elderly. It provides design reference for learning apps for the elderly.

articleTitle: Experiences of Blended Learning using i-LearnV3 Platform in Semiconductor Device Course
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering, Technology and Education (TALE)
abstract: This study was conducted to demonstrate i-LearnV3 as a tool for promoting blended learning (BL) mode in higher education. This research engaged two group (N=41) of Electrical Engineering students who enrolled in a Semiconductor Device course. Positive impacts have been reported regarding the usefulness of i-LearnV3. This paper also focus on the students' acceptance and satisfaction with using online discussion forum and video-based lessons as the components of the BL module in the i-LearnV3 portal.

articleTitle: On the Training Method for the Research Ability of Graduate Students in Engineering
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering, Technology and Education (TALE)
abstract: Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics (STEM) education has been researched all around the world for years and has been proved that it needs knowledgeable and skillful design in all aspects. Many previous research focused on the combination of teaching and practicing, while neglecting the development of research ability of graduate students. So this paper discusses a systematic training method to improve the quality of research from three aspects: how teachers can do to train the research thinking for their students, what the colleges and universities can do to train the research skills for their students, and the ways for undergraduate and graduate students to improve their innovation skills in research.

articleTitle: A Preliminary Study of Using State-Diagram-Based Embedded Programming in a Project-Based Engineering Design Course
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering, Technology and Education (TALE)
abstract: Teaching first-year engineering students in the topics of electronics and control has been a challenging task. Although microcontrollers can be used in junction with an embedded system to allow students to control the hardware using software, students who do not have prior knowledge in software programming will now have to overcome the software hurdle before they can start to learn the hardware. In this paper, a state-diagram-based embedded programming technique is proposed. Preliminary results obtained in trial runs are given to highlight the effectiveness of the proposed methodology when students apply it to project-based learning environment and problem-solving situations.

articleTitle: EEG Based Identification of Words on Exam Models with Yes-No Answers for Students with Visual Impairments
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering, Technology and Education (TALE)
abstract: Education is one of the basic universal human rights. For each level of education, at the end of the learning process, an evaluation was typically carried out through examinations either verbally, written (in the form of either paper-based or computer-based and offline or online) or both. The problem to be faced by visually impaired student is the written exam requires to read the questions and write the answers. This study aims to proposed a novel concept of the test model with Yes-No answers for visual impairments students at elementary level by adopting EEG-based brain computer interface (BCI) technology at elementary level. Data EEG was recorded using Emotiv Epoc from a young man and for classification using Long Short Term Memory (LSTM) with the accuracy 97.75%.

articleTitle: Analysis of Learning Modalities Towards Effective Undergraduate Cybersecurity Education Design
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering, Technology and Education (TALE)
abstract: Cybersecurity education is a critical component of today's computer science and IT curriculum. To provide for a highly effective cybersecurity education, we propose using machine-learning techniques to identify common learning modalities of cybersecurity students in order to optimize how cybersecurity core topics, threats, tools and techniques are taught. We test various hypothesis, e.g. that students of selected VARK learning styles will outperform their peers. The results indicate that for the class assignments in our study preference of read/write and kinesthetic modalities yielded the best results. This further indicates that specific learning instruments can be tailored for students based on their individual VARK learning styles.

articleTitle: Visual learning as Object Recognition to Recognize Image for Mental Disorder Children
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering, Technology and Education (TALE)
abstract: Technology has improved a lot comparing to the previous years. The improvement can be seen from various development of a program that may benefit human life. One example of the advancement of technology is artificial intelligence (AI). AI has taken a considerable part in becoming the primary necessity in computer programming. One famous example of AI is object recognition. An arrangement of codes is established for the machine to recognize a picture that is inputted. Even so, the use of object recognition programs that may help mental disorder children is still low -- considering that they are still in the age where education is crucial. However, the standard approach of teaching them is not the right way to make them understand since they need individual adjustments and appropriate training for them to follow. Therefore. We are proposing an application that will help to educate mental disorder children through the use of object recognition in visual learning. The app will have built-in features such as vocalize the object's name, which will help mental disorder children to know and remember how it is pronounced. Other features to further improve the education has guessed the word and draw the object which will help them to understand how the object is shaped. Moreover, Researches have proved that learning visually will help mental disorder children to understand better.

articleTitle: Graphene Based Futuristic Green Batteries For Energy Harvesting
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering, Technology and Education (TALE)
abstract: The depleting fossil fuels coupled with increasing per capita energy consumption necessitate the scientific community to explore newer recyclable sources of energy harvesting for powering the myriad electrically fed appliances. Graphene is touted to be a material of immense promise in the design of rechargeable batteries of futuristic vision, and hence the need to concisely consolidate the present status of these next generation batteries has been felt. Graphene may be used directly for electrodes, as well as in tandem with other materials for battery applications; due to its excellent intrinsic electrical conductivity, thermal conductivity as well as very high surface area; which result in the enhancement of battery parameters of interest like power density, energy density, thermal management, battery lifetime and compactness. Herein we have consolidated the role of graphene in electrodes of Li-ion batteries, Li-air batteries, as well as flexible graphene-based batteries. This consolidation will serve in optimal design of batteries which are very important for powering multiple utilities.

articleTitle: Interdisciplinary Teaching of Basic Architectural Design Knowledge under the Environmental Design Major: An Exploration
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering, Technology and Education (TALE)
abstract: Interdisciplinary teaching basic architectural knowledge have been adjusted to meet actual demands and highlight instructional characteristics. Through rational material arrangement, the involvement of practical teaching, teaching method and tactic reform, the interdisciplinary teaching of basic architectural design knowledge under the environmental design major can satisfactorily realize the teaching objectives. The teaching setting and reasonable arrangement of architectural basic knowledge course cluster can actively and effectively promote students to master solid professional basic knowledge, principles and design methods, and enable them to have higher artistic accomplishment, innovative design thinking and skilled design expression ability, and apply what they have learned creatively in environmental design practice. The teaching experience of building basic knowledge course cluster can provide a reference case for similar universities to draw up their teaching plan. Now this professional cluster depends on the basic knowledge of construction course, surrounding the applied innovative talents training target, actively explore practical, innovative talent training plan and teaching team construction mode, promote studio practice teaching mode, the characteristics of the combination of formation, highlight the students' innovative spirit, teamwork and comprehensive professional skills, promote students' employment competitiveness. Environmental design professional under the open environment design professional courses in basic knowledge of architectural design, through the reasonable organization of teaching content, the introduction of the practice teaching segment and teaching method reform, to achieve the target, in the limited class hour achieve more ideal teaching, help students to establish the design principle of science, realize the unity of culture and art and engineering technology.

articleTitle: Design Thinking for Computational Creativity – a Case Study of International Exchanges Using Game and Animation (2014-Recent)
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering, Technology and Education (TALE)
abstract: The Asia-Pacific region has been dominating the global video game market for years. In recent years, an increasing number of Indonesia students are turning their interest to study in Taiwan. However, Chinese education in Indonesia is fundamentally based on studies of Mainland China, therefore lacking opportunities for students to understand profoundly Taiwan's language and culture. Furthermore, there is a lack of opportunities for students to understand game design power and industry in Taiwan. The purpose of this on-going program (2014-recent) is to enhance the understanding of game and animation design education in Taiwan, through exchanges with students in Indonesia. It aims to promote exchanges between the faculty and students at the universities with faculties, lecturers and artists in Taiwan for collaborative work, especially in game art design, game engine and animation. It sincerely hopes that students could understand profoundly Taiwan's language and culture by game and animation online tutorials, and provide opportunities for students to understand game design power and industry in Taiwan, Indonesia, and worldwide market. After a year of implementing the four points mentioned in this article, we have already observed some evident outcome. The biggest achievement comes from the workshop which has received significant responses and an increasing number of attendances from both Taiwan and Indonesia. In the near future, it hopes that we can hold a public event such as lecture, workshop and exhibition to raise awareness of and develop an affinity with Taiwanese langue and culture among the general public using the design thinking approach for computational creativity, such as co-design Taiwan language on-line course or game-based learning.

articleTitle: Design Features for Gender-specific Differences in Blended Learning within Higher Education in Indonesia
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering, Technology and Education (TALE)
abstract: Blended learning offers learning solutions for higher educational institutions facing the industrial revolution 4.0. In this study, we investigated the influence factors student perceptions of blended learning based on gender-specific differences in Indonesia. We applied a research model to systematically assess the effect of design features on the effectiveness of blended learning indicators (intrinsic motivation and student satisfaction). Moreover, we evaluated the research model for both genders separately. Based on the quantitative survey of 223 Indonesian students, our study confirms that the design features significantly influence the effectiveness of blended learning for male and female students.

articleTitle: Examining the usage of and access to online databases for academic purposes: A study at an engineering- and technology-based university in Malaysia
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering, Technology and Education (TALE)
abstract: In higher learning processes, information and reference sources are considered significant to both students and staff of higher education institutions (HEIs) in gathering references and reviewing literatures. Currently, students and staff tend to obtain or access references from the online databases and electronic resources provided by their university's libraries. In this study, we examine the number and titles of online databases that are most frequently searched, viewed and downloaded by students and staff for academic purposes. Data were obtained from the annual reports published by the university's library between 2014 and 2017. Findings revealed a high percentage of usage and access per year, which clearly indicates that the students and staff of the university are aware of the online databases provided by the university's library. It was also found that the five titles accessed most frequently by the university's students and staff were: IEEE Xplore Digital Library, ScienceDirect, EdITLib, Datastream and Scopus. In light of these findings, it is recommended that librarians should continuously encourage active and efficient usage of online databases among the students and staff, especially for academic purposes.

articleTitle: Design, Development and Delivery of a Complimentary STEM Program for Primary School Pupils
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering, Technology and Education (TALE)
abstract: Presently, in Singapore and most of the countries, many students have avoided doing STEM courses because it is difficult and it does not pay them well after graduation. The country is experiencing lack of good engineers, technologists and scientists [1], [2]. An initiative has been started to introduce STEM to students at young age in a fun and yet effective learning way. Team TBSS designed and developed a 6-hour STEM targeting pupils between 10 and 12 years old who are reading primary 4 and primary 6 in school. The program has been conducted several times with Henry Park Primary School. The process, findings and experiences will be shared in this paper.

articleTitle: Question Authoring for Learning Programming Skills based on the Programmed Visual Content Comparison Method
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering, Technology and Education (TALE)
abstract: This paper discusses a question authoring function of the Programmed Visual Contents Comparison Method (PVCC). With this method, by comparing two displayed pictures produced by programming samples (a question), a learner must decide which one the programs producing those pictures is the more difficult to build by programming, or if the difficulty is similar for all of them. After the learners answered the sample comparison, the PVCC test system returns the correct answer and detailed explanation of the question to make sure their understanding and improve their skill. A question in the PVCC test is to evaluate and to promote learners' programming skills related to a specific programming concept. Question for the PVCC test is hard to generate automatically because a programming concept is distributed and implicit in a program, and depends on the structure of arbitrary programs. Therefore, we design and prototype an authoring function to store programming samples, to combine samples and generate a question and to organize the test for the PVCC test system.

articleTitle: A Holistic Active Learning Framework
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering, Technology and Education (TALE)
abstract: We introduces the application and effect of a holistic active learning to allow students' explorations of their own attitudes and values. Our four year practice has proved that this teaching method can inspire students' interest, deepen their understanding, improve their engineering ability, and nurture innovative thinking. Furthermore, it develops a positive effect on teaching and assessment reform for all programs.

articleTitle: Engage Your Students Before Class: More Pre-Class Engagement for More Effective Flipped Classrooms
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering, Technology and Education (TALE)
abstract: Lacking student preparation before class has been the most commonly identified challenge when adopting the flipped classroom approach. In this study, we have introduced a class activity which can increase student pre-class online engagement and help them better prepare for the in-class activity. During this activity, students are required to work in small groups before in-class activities to answer open-ended questions related to the course learning materials via an online shared document. Based on teachers' duty, there are four stages for implementation of the proposed activity which are: (1) initiation: teacher needs to design open-ended questions and creates online shared editable documents for each group; (2) scaffolding: teacher assists learners in providing responses by checking their editing logs; (3) assessment: students' access to the online shared documents will be suspended and teacher will evaluate students responses; and (4) reflection: teacher will address common issues and propose more challenging questions before the related in-class activities. We have conducted experiments in the third cohort of a flipped general education course on computational thinking and algorithms. Except for the proposed class activity, the first two cohorts of this course have the same design and content in three topics and therefore worked as control groups. Online interaction data of all three cohorts have been collected for a thorough comparison. Results showed that students' average lecture video access rates have improved in the third cohort compared to the first two cohorts by 49 % and 39 % respectively. The percentage of students who never accessed any lecture videos decreased from around 29 % in the first and second cohorts to 6 % in the third cohort where the proposed activity was implemented. A statistically significant difference was discovered between the first and third cohorts (t = -15.06, p<; 0.00001), and between the second and third cohorts (t = _27.02, p<; 0.00001) of the course in lecture video access rates.

articleTitle: Collaborative Group Learning in Programming Classes
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering, Technology and Education (TALE)
abstract: The first semester at the university level is considered as decisive for a student, especially for an engineering student. This certain period concerns building a base for the student, consequences to reach out to their professional life. To help the students to utilize that time properly, we are proposing an alternative way to practice programming in the lab classes. We are introducing a collaborative group learning approach along with monthly programming contests on some specific topics among them and encouraging them to work as a group. In the beginning, freshers may not feel comfortable to work in a group with new faces but as they are also very young, they will take the competition as a challenge and will work together to get a good result. In this way, they will collaborate and share their knowledge with one another which will help the weak students to gain enough knowledge about the topic. Although the technique may fairly help the sparkling students, it will help the average and below-average students a lot.

articleTitle: A Case Study of Collaborative Mobile Learning in Large-size Classes
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering, Technology and Education (TALE)
abstract: Class size has been considered as an important factor that influences the efficiency of language education. Research has found that collaborative learning and mobile technologies can help improve learning in large-size classes. Under this context, this paper reports an empirical study of integrating collaborative and mobile learning into English courses offered by a 4-year comprehensive university in China. It first introduces a team-based mobile learning model and then reports its implementation in language education among STEM students in large-size classes. The study reveals both challenges and opportunities for implementing collaborative mobile learning in higher educational classes in China.

articleTitle: A Parametric Diffraction Pattern based Game Module Design for the Experiment of Optical Analogy of Reflected Electron Diffraction from One-Dimensional Structures
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering, Technology and Education (TALE)
abstract: In this paper, an example game module design added to an existing STEM experiment kit of reflected optical diffraction is presented for the illustration of wave/particle properties. Showing fascinating diffraction patterns, the kit demonstrates the different reflected diffraction phenomena of a light beam from laser diode illuminated on the samples with non-uniform grating (or one-dimensional surface modulations). Extracting the parameters of the diffraction patterns generated, namely φ the angle of rotation of the sample and; θ the angle of incidence of the laser beam relative to the surface of the sample; the parametric diffraction pattern based game module design approach is presented with few examples of φ is 30°, 60° as well as 90° and; this approach is anticipated to contribute to the increase of study motivation of the experiment kit used for the teaching of science of diffraction.

articleTitle: The Development of Innovative Blended Learning System Using Manga to Improve the Cross Cultural Communication
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering, Technology and Education (TALE)
abstract: We have been developing the innovative e-learning system using Manga for international students. We have blended a variety of learning events and have built up the original training method of the cross-cultural communication to cultivate mindset and skillset. We have solved the several problems of existing teaching materials to learn the cross cultural communication. And we have evaluated the effect of the learning system. After learning several courses on our e-learning system, each international student had a test to check the ability of the cross cultural communication. By analyzing a lot of feedback from our users who are international students and educational institutions, we were able to confirm that we had solved the several problems of existing teaching materials. And, we were able to confirm the learning effectiveness of our e-learning by comparing the international students who had learned with the ones who had not learned. We describe the result that we have investigated the effectiveness of the e-learning system for international students to learn cross-cultural understanding through Japanese domestic business manner.

articleTitle: Addressing the Literacy Skills of B40 Students towards 4IR Workplace: Development of FutureProof Graduate Module (FPGM)
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering, Technology and Education (TALE)
abstract: It has been the aspiration of most Malaysian higher learning institutions to produce holistic and balanced graduates that are highly competent to suit the demands of the Fourth Industrial Revolution (4IR). Despite their increasing efforts, various issues concerning local graduates' lack of critical thinking, communication skills and English literacy remain unsettled. This study aims to examine the literacy skills of a large number of students at Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia (UKM), who are considered as `at-risk' students, given their background from the B40 category while they also obtained a low level of English proficiency (MUET Band 1-3). It intends to examine their existing literacy skills in relation to the required skills of the 4IR including communication, Information and Communication Technology (ICT), technology literacy, problem solving and teamwork. This study employed a qualitative research method incorporating secondary data and data collated from an online survey. It is expected to contribute to the enhancement of body of knowledge on Malaysian graduates' employability for the 4IR. It is hoped that the Future-Proof Graduate Module (FPGM) that will be developed from this study will intensify the employability prospects of all students from the B40 category.

articleTitle: Lecture Notes on the Application of Eigenvalue Decomposition in Signal Processing
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering, Technology and Education (TALE)
abstract: Eigenvalue decomposition is one of the important signal reconstruction methods in high-dimensional space, which is of great significance in the field of signal processing. Here, through eigenvalue decomposition, we discuss the difference between the deterministic signal and the random signal in filter, the difference between the signal fitting and the periodic spectrum estimation, the advantages of multidimensional scaling analysis compared to traditional positioning methods, and the differences between reference and surveillance channels' estimation methods. This lecture notes show that eigenvalue decomposition is not only a mathematical tool, but also a way of thinking from high-dimensional to low-dimensional. The comparative study of interrelated methods is conducive to students' understanding and mastery of these methods, and more importantly, provides students with a learning idea.

articleTitle: Mind Map for Task-Oriented Teaching of “Digital System Design”
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering, Technology and Education (TALE)
abstract: In the teaching of “Digital System Design”, taskoriented teaching methodology, where lectures are organized based on tasks, is effective to consolidate students’ mindset of hardware design and improve students’ performance. However, this teaching method scrambles the knowledge points, i.e., a particular topic is not introduced systematically as a whole; instead, some points of the topic are introduced with a task, while some other points of the topic are introduced with some other tasks. This may cause difficulties for some students to systematically study the subject. In this paper, we propose to use mind map to recover the systematism of the task-oriented teaching method, such that students can enjoy the effectiveness of the teaching method, but meanwhile are not affected by its out-of-order introduction of knowledge points.

articleTitle: Indonesia Teacher Engagement Index (ITEI) Intervention: An Effective Video Framework
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering, Technology and Education (TALE)
abstract: The Indonesian Teacher Engagement Index is an instrument used to look at the picture of teacher engagement conditions that are relevant to the Indonesian context. The research that has been conducted since 2015 has reached the stage of providing interventions for teachers who have conducted self-assessments and obtained a picture of their internal profile that refers to the six dimensions. The instruments that have been developed in the form of applications and websites require interventions that are also in accordance with technological developments. This study aims to apply the video to the website that has been developed so that it will be easily accessed and used by teachers to increase the level of engagement in themselves directly. The recommended video will depend on the results of the teacher profiling based on the dimensions of the ITEI benchmark. To optimize intervention, video selection will help teachers increase engagement according to their needs.

articleTitle: Illustrating Engineering Education: A Children’s Book to Support STEM Outreach in Qatar
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering, Technology and Education (TALE)
abstract: In recent years, increased attention has been placed on improving STEM curricula to promote lifelong learning to children at a young age. Integrating STEM topics in children's literature is an effective way to convey knowledge as it combines creativity, motivation and inquisitiveness. Due to the lack of children's literature on engineering in the Middle East region, stories that young children can relate to - in terms of their traditions, culture, and region - and at the same time introduces them to the field of engineering would be of great value to the educational system. With that in mind, a model program was initiated at Texas A&M University at Qatar where undergraduate engineering students worked on a yearlong project to create an illustrated storybook about how drinkable water is produced in a desert nation where fresh water is scarce using engineering. This paper discusses the process of how this project came to fruition.

articleTitle: Internet Protocol Multimedia Subsystem Security Risk Mitigation In Fix Telephone Network
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering, Technology and Education (TALE)
abstract: IP Multimedia Subsystem (IMS) is core networks of enhance telecommunication technology which running over the open platform and Internet Protocols (IP). Hence the security risks from open platform and IP Networks contribute to the Risk of IMS technology usage. Appropriate safeguards need to developed in order IMS technology can be used safely and provide it services. The purpose of this study is to get a security risks profile in the implementation and operation of IMS on fixed telephone networks and develop the comprehensive security mitigation strategy. To obtain a complete risk profile, it required trusted and reliable risk assessment framework. The author chooses the framework of National Institute of Standard and Technology (NIST) Special Publication 800-30, which provides complete guidance in obtaining risk assessments. The result of the risk assessment becomes an input to develop mitigation strategies. Appropriate mitigation strategies derived from the risk profile and suitability of actions that need to be done. Security Mitigation plan are taken to reduce the risks that may occur. Mitigation can be achieved through comprehensive implementation of security controls in technical, managerial, and operational. With the implementation of comprehensive control of security risk reduction will be achieved.

articleTitle: Students’ Fixation on Tables in PowerPoint Slides
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering, Technology and Education (TALE)
abstract: In this research, we reveal the way students read slides. We intimately record the interaction between the students and the slides by an eye-tracking device. From the data, we trace the students' gazing points from one word to another word, sentence to sentence. The study involves 30 sophomores and junior students learning materials presented on 52 slides. Some notabled results are the following. Most students gaze to all words on each slide on the first 20 slides only. Afterward, the number of gazed words decreases quickly and linearly with time. In some cases, 50% of students scan the information with improper order, potentially leading to an incorrect understanding. However, the proportion is reduced by 17% on the average when the slides are designed with a zebra-striping pattern.

articleTitle: Inheritance and Protection Strategies for Tibetan Folk Chess Under the Background of “Internet+”
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering, Technology and Education (TALE)
abstract: Compared to Go, Chess and other chess played by many people, Tibetan chess are mostly played in Tibetan areas. Tibetan chess, especially Tibetan Go, is becoming extinction.To protect it, more and more attention must be paid to its inheritance and protection. Under the background of “Internet+”, great changes have taken place in the ways of inheritance and protection of intangible cultural heritage. This paper proposed strategies on inheritance and protection for Tibetan chess. Firstly, the status quo of Tibetan folk chess development is analyzed and the existing problems are concluded. Then Some prospective and practical strategies on inheritance and protection for Tibetan chess are put forward aiming at solve these problems.

articleTitle: Audio Rendering of Mathematical Expressions for Blind Students: a comparative study between MathML and Latex
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering, Technology and Education (TALE)
abstract: Mathematics is an integral and essential part of Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics (STEM) education and Engineering education. Learning mathematics enhances professional career development in technical and economic disciplines. Mathematics is a visual subject because of its graphical and non-linear nature and students with vision impairments (SVI's) gets disadvantaged as they fail to completely comprehend the subject. As a result, they lag behind academically and professionally. With the advent of various assistive technologies and e-learning tools, it is possible to present mathematics in a non-visual way to the SVI's. However, those tools are not intelligent enough to deliver the correct meaning of the mathematical expressions (ME) and cause confusion to the targeted students. The screen readers, for example reads the mathematical content in a linear way as text which is an incorrect way of interpreting ME's and causes confusion. In order to present mathematics in an audio way, two things should be achieved; ease of understanding the output speech and navigation facility to move between various elements of a ME. The two most common mathematical languages used for audio rendering of ME's are MathML and Latex.
